### Current Trajectory Average Income at Year 20: $20.5K {#sec-current_trajectory_avg_income_year_20}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Average income (GDP per capita) at year 20 under current trajectory trajectory.

**Inputs**:

- [Current Trajectory GDP at Year 20](#sec-current_trajectory_gdp_year_20) 🔢: $188T
- [Global Population 2045 (Projected)](#sec-global_population_2045_projected) 📊: 9.2 billion of people

$$
\begin{gathered}
\bar{y}_{base,20} \\
= \frac{GDP_{base,20}}{Pop_{2045}} \\
= \frac{\$188T}{9.2B} \\
= \$20.5K
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
GDP_{base,20} = GDP_0(1+g_{base})^{20}
$$
*✓ High confidence*

### Total Annual Decentralized Framework for Drug Assessment Operational Costs: $40M {#sec-dfda_annual_opex}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Total annual Decentralized Framework for Drug Assessment operational costs (sum of all components: platform + staff + infra + regulatory + community)

**Inputs**:

- [Decentralized Framework for Drug Assessment Maintenance Costs](#sec-dfda_opex_platform_maintenance): $15M (95% CI: $10M - $22M)
- [Decentralized Framework for Drug Assessment Staff Costs](#sec-dfda_opex_staff): $10M (95% CI: $7M - $15M)
- [Decentralized Framework for Drug Assessment Infrastructure Costs](#sec-dfda_opex_infrastructure): $8M (95% CI: $5M - $12M)
- [Decentralized Framework for Drug Assessment Regulatory Coordination Costs](#sec-dfda_opex_regulatory): $5M (95% CI: $3M - $8M)
- [Decentralized Framework for Drug Assessment Community Support Costs](#sec-dfda_opex_community): $2M (95% CI: $1M - $3M)

$$
\begin{gathered}
OPEX_{dFDA} \\
= Cost_{platform} + Cost_{staff} + Cost_{infra} \\
+ Cost_{regulatory} + Cost_{community} \\
= \$15M + \$10M + \$8M + \$5M + \$2M \\
= \$40M
\end{gathered}
$$

*✓ High confidence*

### Maximum Trial Capacity Multiplier (Physical Limit): 566x {#sec-dfda_max_trial_capacity_multiplier_physical}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Physical upper bound on trial-capacity multiplier from participant availability. Even with unlimited funding, annual trial enrollment cannot exceed willing participant pool.

**Inputs**:

- [Global Patients Willing to Participate in Clinical Trials](#sec-willing_trial_participants_global) 🔢: 1.08 billion people
- [Annual Global Clinical Trial Participants](#sec-current_trial_slots_available) 📊: 1.9 million patients/year (95% CI: 1.5 million patients/year - 2.3 million patients/year)

$$
\begin{gathered}
k_{capacity,max} \\
= \frac{N_{willing}}{Slots_{curr}} \\
= \frac{1.08B}{1.9M} \\
= 566
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
N_{willing} \\
= N_{patients} \times Pct_{willing} \\
= 2.4B \times 44.8\% \\
= 1.08B
\end{gathered}
$$
*~ Medium confidence*

#### Sensitivity Analysis

### dFDA Patients Fundable Annually: 23.4 million patients/year {#sec-dfda_patients_fundable_annually}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Number of patients fundable annually from dFDA funding at pragmatic trial cost. Source-agnostic counterpart of DIH_PATIENTS_FUNDABLE_ANNUALLY.

**Inputs**:

- [dFDA Annual Trial Subsidies](#sec-dfda_trial_subsidies_annual) 🔢: $21.8B
- [dFDA Pragmatic Trial Cost per Patient](#sec-dfda_pragmatic_trial_cost_per_patient) 📊: $929 (95% CI: $97 - $3K)

$$
\begin{gathered}
N_{fundable,dFDA} \\
= \frac{Subsidies_{dFDA,ann}}{Cost_{pragmatic,pt}} \\
= \frac{\$21.8B}{\$929} \\
= 23.4M
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
Subsidies_{dFDA,ann} \\
= Funding_{dFDA,ann} - OPEX_{dFDA} \\
= \$21.8B - \$40M \\
= \$21.8B
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
OPEX_{dFDA} \\
= Cost_{platform} + Cost_{staff} + Cost_{infra} \\
+ Cost_{regulatory} + Cost_{community} \\
= \$15M + \$10M + \$8M + \$5M + \$2M \\
= \$40M
\end{gathered}
$$
*✓ High confidence*

### Diseases Without Effective Treatment: 6.65 thousand diseases {#sec-diseases_without_effective_treatment}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Number of diseases without effective treatment. 95% of 7,000 rare diseases lack FDA-approved treatment (per Orphanet 2024). This represents the therapeutic search space that remains unexplored.

**Inputs**:

- [Total Number of Rare Diseases Globally](#sec-rare_diseases_count_global) 📊: 7 thousand diseases (95% CI: 6 thousand diseases - 10 thousand diseases)

$$
\begin{gathered}
N_{untreated} \\
= N_{rare} \times 0.95 \\
= 7{,}000 \times 0.95 \\
= 6{,}650
\end{gathered}

### Global Opportunity Cost Total: $101T {#sec-political_dysfunction_global_opportunity_cost_total}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Total global opportunity cost from governance failures: health innovation delays ($34T), underfunded science ($4T), lead poisoning ($6T), migration restrictions ($57T). Sum: $101T annually in unrealized potential.

**Inputs**:

- [Global Health Opportunity Cost](#sec-political_dysfunction_global_health_opportunity_cost) 📊: $34T (95% CI: $20T - $80T)
- [Global Science Opportunity Cost](#sec-political_dysfunction_global_science_opportunity_cost) 📊: $4T (95% CI: $2T - $10T)
- [Global Lead Poisoning Cost](#sec-political_dysfunction_global_lead_opportunity_cost) 📊: $6T (95% CI: $4T - $8T)
- [Global Migration Opportunity Cost](#sec-political_dysfunction_global_migration_opportunity_cost) 📊: $57T (95% CI: $57T - $170T)

$$
\begin{gathered}
O_{total} \\
= O_{health} + O_{science} + O_{lead} + O_{migration} \\
= \$34T + \$4T + \$6T + \$57T \\
= \$101T
\end{gathered}
$$

**Methodology**: [@political-dysfunction-tax-paper-2025]

*? Low confidence*

### Percentage Military Spending Cut After WW2: 87.6% {#sec-post_ww2_military_cut_pct}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Percentage US military spending cut after WW2 (1945-1947, inflation-adjusted: $1,420B to $176B in constant 2024 dollars)

**Inputs**:

- [US Military Spending in 1947 (Constant 2024 Dollars)](#sec-us_military_spending_1947_annual_2024usd) 📊: $176B
- [US Military Spending at WW2 Peak (Constant 2024 Dollars)](#sec-us_military_spending_1945_peak_annual_2024usd) 📊: $1.42T

$$
\begin{gathered}
Cut_{WW2} \\
= 1 - \frac{Spending_{US,1947}}{Spending_{US,1945}} \\
= 1 - \frac{\$176B}{\$1.42T} \\
= 87.6\%
\end{gathered}
$$

*✓ High confidence*

:::

### Wishonia Disease Cure Fraction (20yr, Full Implementation): 100% {#sec-wishonia_disease_cure_fraction_20yr_full}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Wishonia disease-cure fraction over 20 years under full implementation. Uses full trial-capacity scaling and applies an upper bound of 100% of untreated disease classes.

**Inputs**:

- [Diseases Getting First Treatment Per Year](#sec-new_disease_first_treatments_per_year) 📊: 15 diseases/year (95% CI: 8 diseases/year - 30 diseases/year)
- [Trial Capacity Multiplier](#sec-dfda_trial_capacity_multiplier) 🔢: 12.3x
- [Wishonia Military Reallocation Physical Max Share](#sec-wishonia_military_reallocation_physical_max_share) 🔢: 87.6%
- [Maximum Trial Capacity Multiplier (Physical Limit)](#sec-dfda_max_trial_capacity_multiplier_physical) 🔢: 566x
- [Diseases Without Effective Treatment](#sec-diseases_without_effective_treatment) 🔢: 6.65 thousand diseases

$$
\begin{gathered}
f_{cure,20,wish} \\
= \min\left(1,\frac{Treatments_{new,ann}\cdot k_{capacity,wish}\cdot 20}{D_{untreated}}\right)
\end{gathered}
$$

*✓ High confidence*

:::

### Wishonia Trajectory GDP at Year 20: $10.7 quadrillion {#sec-wishonia_trajectory_gdp_year_20}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Projected global GDP at year 20 under the Wishonia Trajectory. Model applies all Wishonia policy channels and redirects the full Political Dysfunction Tax non-health opportunity pool to highest-marginal-value uses. Health recovery is modeled separately through disease burden removal to avoid overlap. Military and non-health reallocation effects are ramped at 50% intensity for the first 3 years, then 100% for years 4-20, reflecting implementation lag. Military reallocation uses a physically demonstrated upper bound (post-WW2 demobilization) rather than an arbitrary policy cap.

**Inputs**:

- [Global GDP (2025)](#sec-global_gdp_2025) 📊: $115T
- [Baseline Global GDP Growth Rate](#sec-gdp_baseline_growth_rate): 2.5%
- [Wishonia Military Reallocation Physical Max Share](#sec-wishonia_military_reallocation_physical_max_share) 🔢: 87.6%
- [GDP Growth Boost at 30% Military Reallocation](#sec-military_redirect_gdp_boost_at_30pct): 5.5% (95% CI: 3.5% - 7.5%)
- [R&D Spillover Multiplier](#sec-rd_spillover_multiplier): 2x (95% CI: 1.5x - 2.5x)
- [Wishonia Disease Cure Fraction (20yr, Full Implementation)](#sec-wishonia_disease_cure_fraction_20yr_full) 🔢: 100%
- [Disease Burden as % of GDP](#sec-disease_burden_gdp_drag_pct) 📊: 13%
- [Global Science Opportunity Cost](#sec-political_dysfunction_global_science_opportunity_cost) 📊: $4T (95% CI: $2T - $10T)

### Disease Burden as % of GDP: 13% {#sec-disease_burden_gdp_drag_pct}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Fraction of GDP currently lost to disease (productivity losses + medical costs diverted from productive use). $5T productivity loss + $9.9T direct medical costs = $14.9T on $115T GDP = ~13%. As diseases are progressively cured, this drag is recovered as GDP growth. This is the missing factor that makes the treaty trajectory look like a singularity rather than a modest improvement.

**Source**: [@disease-economic-burden-109t]

#### Uncertainty Range

**Technical**: Distribution: Fixed

*✓ High confidence*

:::

### Global Health Opportunity Cost: $34T {#sec-political_dysfunction_global_health_opportunity_cost}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Annual opportunity cost of slow-motion regulatory environment for health innovation. Murphy-Topel (2006) valued cancer cure at $50T (inflation-adjusted ~$100T in 2025). Longevity dividend of 1 extra year = $38T globally. PCTs could accelerate cures by 10+ years; NPV of 10-year delay at 3% discount = ~$25T. Conservative estimate: $34T annually in lives lost and healthspan denied.

**Source**: [@political-dysfunction-tax-paper-2025]

#### Uncertainty Range

**Technical**: 95% CI: [$20T, $80T] • Distribution: Lognormal (SE: $15T)

**What this means**: This estimate is highly uncertain. The true value likely falls between $20T and $80T (±88%). This represents a very wide range that our Monte Carlo simulations account for when calculating overall uncertainty in the results.

*The lognormal distribution means values can't go negative and have a longer tail toward higher values (common for costs and populations).*

#### Input Distribution

{{< include ../figures/distribution-political_dysfunction_global_health_opportunity_cost.qmd >}}

:::

### Global Migration Opportunity Cost: $57T {#sec-political_dysfunction_global_migration_opportunity_cost}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Unrealized output from migration restrictions. Clemens (2011) calculated eliminating labor mobility barriers could increase global GDP by 50-150%. At $115T global GDP, lower bound = $57T; upper bound = $170T. Even 5% workforce mobility would generate trillions, exceeding all foreign aid ever given. This is the largest single distortion in the global economy.

**Source**: [@political-dysfunction-tax-paper-2025]

#### Uncertainty Range

**Technical**: 95% CI: [$57T, $170T] • Distribution: Lognormal (SE: $30T)

**What this means**: This estimate is highly uncertain. The true value likely falls between $57T and $170T (±99%). This represents a very wide range that our Monte Carlo simulations account for when calculating overall uncertainty in the results.

*The lognormal distribution means values can't go negative and have a longer tail toward higher values (common for costs and populations).*

#### Input Distribution

{{< include ../figures/distribution-political_dysfunction_global_migration_opportunity_cost.qmd >}}

*? Low confidence*

:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Annual opportunity cost from underfunding high-ROI science (fusion, AI safety). Human Genome Project: $3.8B cost, $796B-1T impact (141:1 ROI). Fusion DEMO plant: $5-10B could solve energy/climate permanently. AI safety: <5% of capabilities spending despite existential stakes. Reallocating $200B from military waste at 20x multiplier = $4T foregone growth.
